requirements.text: A web service in the language's usual minimal framework with one endpoint, GET /books?category=<name>, that runs the crawl when called.
The crawl finds the named category on books.toscrape.com and follows its "next" pages to the end.
The endpoint answers the category's books as JSON, each with its title and price.
Two calls running at once in the same process do not interfere: each has its own Run/Crawler, results and state.
Calling it again later works the same: nothing process-wide is consumed or left unrestartable.
If the caller disconnects, the crawl stops and every connection and browser it used is released.
The library's logs go to the service's own logger and nothing is printed to standard output (no library-installed handlers or signal handlers).
The same crawl is also called from a Python notebook cell (on its running loop without blocking or failing) and from a plain script in TypeScript and Rust.

api_misuses.assumed: a client crate whose Client::new(ClientConfig) opens a connection
api_misuses.doc_says: no such crate or types; the connection is Foxhound::connect(ConnectOptions)

api_misuses.assumed: a crawl bound to a client
api_misuses.doc_says: Crawl::new() takes no arguments; a Run is started with Foxhound::start_crawl(&crawl, seeds)

api_misuses.assumed: built-in scenario-specific settings that pick the category and page
api_misuses.doc_says: Crawl has no settings field; the crawl is declared with labels, handlers, datasets and seeds

api_misuses.assumed: a call that crawls one page and returns its books
api_misuses.doc_says: no run() on Crawl and no CrawlResult type; records are read from the Run's Dataset after serve()
not needed; unused import of a member not used by the program

programs.notes: The program invents a client crate, a settings object and a run() returning books, none of which exist in the stubs, so no crawl would happen; the axum handler also takes a bare String instead of the query extractor and returns a non-JSON Vec, uses axum::Server (removed in axum 0.7), unwraps errors, and has no disconnect handling, no closing, and no plain-script mode.
